title: A Complete Classification of Maximal Hyperelliptic Curves Related to Chebyshev Polynomials

definitions.name: x2611_14198_point_count
definitions.lean:
noncomputable def x2611_14198_point_count (d p r : ℕ) [Fact p.Prime] : ℕ :=
  Nat.card {xy : GaloisField p r × GaloisField p r //
    xy.2 ^ 2 = (Polynomial.Chebyshev.C (GaloisField p r) (d : ℤ)).eval xy.1} +
    if d % 2 = 0 then 2 else 1
definitions.notes: Number of points of the smooth projective model of y² = φ_d(x) over F_(p^r), used only for d ≥ 3, r ≥ 1 and p ∤ 2d. Mathlib Polynomial.Chebyshev.C has exactly the paper’s normalization φ_d = 2T_d(x/2). The affine solution count has one rational point at infinity for odd d and two for even d, since φ_d is monic and squarefree under these hypotheses. Nat.card avoids choosing a Fintype instance.

definitions.name: x2611_14198_maximal
definitions.notes: Equality with the upper Hasse–Weil bound. The genus is the printed floor((d−1)/2); real square root allows every positive extension degree, without assuming evenness as an extra hypothesis.

definitions.name: x2611_14198_minimal
definitions.notes: Equality with the lower Hasse–Weil bound, with subtraction in ℝ rather than truncated natural subtraction.

definitions.name: x2611_14198_character_sum
definitions.lean:
noncomputable def x2611_14198_character_sum (d : ℕ) (χ : DirichletCharacter ℂ d) : ℂ :=
  ∑ a ∈ Finset.Icc 1 ((d - 1) / 2), (-1 : ℂ) ^ (a + 1) * χ (a : ZMod d)
definitions.notes: The sum S_d(χ) from (23); Mathlib Dirichlet characters already vanish on nonunits.

definitions.name: x2611_14198_twist
definitions.lean:
noncomputable def x2611_14198_twist (d : ℕ) (χ : DirichletCharacter ℂ d) : DirichletCharacter ℂ (4 * d) :=
  DirichletCharacter.changeLevel (Nat.dvd_mul_left d 4) χ *
    DirichletCharacter.changeLevel (Nat.dvd_mul_right 4 d)
      (ZMod.χ₄.ringHomComp (Int.castRingHom ℂ))
definitions.notes: χχ₄ regarded as a character modulo 4d, as explicitly required in Lemma 4.2. Both factors are lifted to that modulus with Mathlib changeLevel. χ₄ is Mathlib’s existing nontrivial character modulo 4, composed with ℤ → ℂ.

statements.label: Theorem 1.1 (conditions (2) and (3))
statements.name: x2611_14198_thm1_1_maximal
statements.original:
Let $d\geq 3$ be odd and let $p\nmid 2d$ be a prime with
 $p\equiv 1\pmod{4}$ . The following conditions are equivalent:

(1) 

 $\operatorname{Jac}(\mathcal{H}_{d})$ is supersingular;

(2) 

 $\mathcal{H}_{d}$ is maximal over some finite extension of $\mathbb{F}_{p}$ ;

(3) 

 $d=\ell^{n}$ for a prime $\ell\equiv 1\pmod{4}$ and an integer
 $n\geq 1$ , and $p$ generates $(\mathbb{Z}/\ell^{n}\mathbb{Z})^{\times}$ .
statements.lean: (d p : ℕ) [Fact p.Prime] (hd : 3 ≤ d) (hodd : Odd d) (hcop : ¬ p ∣ 2 * d) (hp : p % 4 = 1) : (∃ r : ℕ, 1 ≤ r ∧ x2611_14198_maximal d p r) ↔ (∃ (ℓ n : ℕ), ℓ.Prime ∧ ℓ % 4 = 1 ∧ 1 ≤ n ∧ d = ℓ ^ n ∧ IsPrimitiveRoot (p : ZMod (ℓ ^ n)) (Nat.totient (ℓ ^ n)))
statements.notes: Selected the equivalence of printed conditions (2) and (3); the equivalence with condition (1), involving supersingular Jacobians, is listed in skipped. Primality is an instance hypothesis Fact p.Prime. IsPrimitiveRoot of order φ(ℓ^n) is exactly generation of the unit group. Maximality is expressed by the actual projective point count, including infinity, rather than an uninterpreted predicate.

fidelity.twin: (d p : ℕ) (hd : 3 ≤ d) (hodd : Odd d) [Fact p.Prime] (hpnd : ¬ p ∣ 2 * d) (hpmod : p % 4 = 1) : (∃ r : ℕ, 1 ≤ r ∧ x2611_14198_maximal d p r) ↔ ∃ ℓ n : ℕ, ℓ.Prime ∧ ℓ % 4 = 1 ∧ 1 ≤ n ∧ d = ℓ ^ n ∧ IsPrimitiveRoot (p : ZMod (ℓ ^ n)) (Nat.totient (ℓ ^ n))

statements.label: Theorem 1.2 (maximal and minimal extension degrees)
statements.name: x2611_14198_thm1_2_fields
statements.original:
Let $\ell\equiv 1\pmod{4}$ and $p\equiv 1\pmod{4}$ be distinct primes, let
 $n\geq 1$ , and suppose that $p$ generates $(\mathbb{Z}/\ell^{n}\mathbb{Z})^{\times}$ . Put

 $m_{j}=\ell^{j-1}(\ell-1)\qquad(1\leq j\leq n).$ 

Then

(2)

 $P_{\mathcal{H}_{\ell^{n}},p}(X)=\prod_{j=1}^{n}\left(X^{m_{j}}+p^{m_{j}/2}\right).$ 

For a positive integer $r$ , the curve $\mathcal{H}_{\ell^{n}}$ is maximal over
 $\mathbb{F}_{p^{r}}$ if and only if $r=m_{n}b$ with $b$ positive and odd. It is
minimal over $\mathbb{F}_{p^{r}}$ if and only if $r=2m_{n}b$ with $b\geq 1$ .
statements.lean: (ℓ p n : ℕ) [Fact ℓ.Prime] [Fact p.Prime] (hℓ : ℓ % 4 = 1) (hp : p % 4 = 1) (hne : ℓ ≠ p) (hn : 1 ≤ n) (hgen : IsPrimitiveRoot (p : ZMod (ℓ ^ n)) (Nat.totient (ℓ ^ n))) (r : ℕ) (hr : 1 ≤ r) : (x2611_14198_maximal (ℓ ^ n) p r ↔ ∃ b : ℕ, 1 ≤ b ∧ Odd b ∧ r = (ℓ ^ (n - 1) * (ℓ - 1)) * b) ∧ (x2611_14198_minimal (ℓ ^ n) p r ↔ ∃ b : ℕ, 1 ≤ b ∧ r = 2 * (ℓ ^ (n - 1) * (ℓ - 1)) * b)
statements.notes: Both printed extension-degree assertions are retained, with m_n expanded. The Frobenius polynomial identity (2) is separately skipped because its characteristic polynomial of a Jacobian requires theory beyond Mathlib. The minimal-field parameter b has no parity restriction, exactly as printed.

fidelity.twin: (ℓ p n r : ℕ) (hℓ : ℓ.Prime) [Fact p.Prime] (hℓmod : ℓ % 4 = 1) (hpmod : p % 4 = 1) (hne : ℓ ≠ p) (hn : 1 ≤ n) (hgen : orderOf (p : ZMod (ℓ ^ n)) = Nat.totient (ℓ ^ n)) (hr : 1 ≤ r) : (x2611_14198_maximal (ℓ ^ n) p r ↔ ∃ b : ℕ, 1 ≤ b ∧ Odd b ∧ r = (ℓ ^ (n - 1) * (ℓ - 1)) * b) ∧ (x2611_14198_minimal (ℓ ^ n) p r ↔ ∃ b : ℕ, 1 ≤ b ∧ r = 2 * (ℓ ^ (n - 1) * (ℓ - 1)) * b)

statements.label: Theorem 1.3 (classification)
statements.name: x2611_14198_thm1_3
statements.original:
Let $p\equiv 1\pmod{4}$ be prime, let $d\geq 4$ be even, and assume
 $p\nmid 2d$ . Then $\mathcal{H}_{d}$ is maximal over some finite extension of
 $\mathbb{F}_{p}$ if and only if one of the following holds:

(1) 

 $d=4$ and $p\equiv 5\pmod{8}$ ;

(2) 

 $d=2\ell^{a}$ , where $\ell\equiv 1\pmod{4}$ is prime, $a\geq 1$ , and
 $p$ generates $(\mathbb{Z}/\ell^{a}\mathbb{Z})^{\times}$ .

In case (1), the maximal fields are precisely $\mathbb{F}_{p^{2b}}$ with
 $b$ positive and odd. In case (2), if
 $M=\ell^{a-1}(\ell-1)$ , they are precisely $\mathbb{F}_{p^{Mb}}$ with $b$ 
positive and odd.
statements.lean: (d p : ℕ) [Fact p.Prime] (hp : p % 4 = 1) (hd : 4 ≤ d) (heven : Even d) (hcop : ¬ p ∣ 2 * d) : (∃ r : ℕ, 1 ≤ r ∧ x2611_14198_maximal d p r) ↔ ((d = 4 ∧ p % 8 = 5) ∨ (∃ (ℓ a : ℕ), ℓ.Prime ∧ ℓ % 4 = 1 ∧ 1 ≤ a ∧ d = 2 * ℓ ^ a ∧ IsPrimitiveRoot (p : ZMod (ℓ ^ a)) (Nat.totient (ℓ ^ a))))
statements.notes: The two printed alternatives are formalized literally. The two subsequent assertions identifying all maximal fields are separate worklist entries.

statements.label: Lemma 4.2 (formula (24))
statements.name: x2611_14198_lem4_2_identity
statements.original:
Let $d>1$ be odd and $\chi$ an even Dirichlet character modulo $d$ .
Then

(24)

 $S_{d}(\chi)=-\frac{\chi_{4}(d)}{\chi(2)}L(0,\chi\chi_{4}),$ 

where the product is regarded as a character modulo $4d$ .
If $\chi$ is primitive and nontrivial, then $\eta=\chi\chi_{4}$ is
primitive and odd, $L(0,\eta)\neq 0$ , and hence $S_{d}(\chi)\neq 0$ .
statements.lean: (d : ℕ) [NeZero d] (hd : 1 < d) (hodd : Odd d) (χ : DirichletCharacter ℂ d) (heven : χ.Even) : x2611_14198_character_sum d χ = -((ZMod.χ₄ (d : ZMod 4) : ℤ) : ℂ) / χ (2 : ZMod d) * DirichletCharacter.LFunction (x2611_14198_twist d χ) 0
statements.notes: Uses Mathlib’s analytically continued LFunction evaluated at the complex number zero, not the divergent defining Dirichlet series. The character product has precisely modulus 4d. The redundant NeZero d instance follows from d > 1 and only supplies Mathlib’s LFunction instance requirement.

fidelity.twin: (d : ℕ) (hd : 1 < d) (hd_odd : Odd d) (χ : DirichletCharacter ℂ d) (hχ : χ.Even) : x2611_14198_character_sum d χ = -((ZMod.χ₄ (d : ZMod 4) : ℂ) / χ (2 : ZMod d)) * @DirichletCharacter.LFunction (4 * d) ⟨by omega⟩ (x2611_14198_twist d χ) 0

(24)

If $\chi$ is primitive and nontrivial, then $\eta=\chi\chi_{4}$ is

statements.label: Lemma 4.3
statements.name: x2611_14198_lem4_3
statements.original:
If $d=\ell^{n}$ with $\ell\equiv 1\pmod{4}$ prime, then $S_{d}(1)=0$ ,
where $1$ denotes the principal character modulo $d$ . For every
nonprincipal even character $\chi$ modulo $d$ , one has $S_{d}(\chi)\neq 0$ .
statements.lean: (ℓ n : ℕ) [Fact ℓ.Prime] (hℓ : ℓ % 4 = 1) : x2611_14198_character_sum (ℓ ^ n) (1 : DirichletCharacter ℂ (ℓ ^ n)) = 0 ∧ ∀ χ : DirichletCharacter ℂ (ℓ ^ n), χ ≠ 1 → χ.Even → x2611_14198_character_sum (ℓ ^ n) χ ≠ 0
statements.notes: Prime-power level d = ℓ^n is substituted throughout. This lemma prints no explicit positive lower bound on n, so the natural exponent also permits n = 0; the sum is empty at that level. The principal character vanishes on nonunits in Mathlib.

fidelity.twin: (d ℓ n : ℕ) (hℓ : Nat.Prime ℓ) (hℓ_mod_four : ℓ % 4 = 1) (hn : 1 ≤ n) (hd : d = ℓ ^ n) : x2611_14198_character_sum d (1 : DirichletCharacter ℂ d) = 0 ∧ ∀ χ : DirichletCharacter ℂ d, χ ≠ 1 → χ.Even → x2611_14198_character_sum d χ ≠ 0

statements.label: Corollary 5.4 (point count)
statements.name: x2611_14198_cor5_4_points
statements.original:
Under the hypotheses of Theorem 1.2, for every $r\geq 1$ ,

 $\#\mathcal{H}_{\ell^{n}}(\mathbb{F}_{p^{r}})=p^{r}+1-\sum_{\begin{subarray}{c}1\leq j\leq n\\
m_{j}\mid r\end{subarray}}m_{j}(-1)^{r/m_{j}}p^{r/2}.$ 

and $J_{\ell^{n}}(\mathbb{F}_{p})[2^{\infty}]\simeq(\mathbb{Z}/2\mathbb{Z})^{n}$ .
statements.lean: (ℓ p n : ℕ) [Fact ℓ.Prime] [Fact p.Prime] (hℓ : ℓ % 4 = 1) (hp : p % 4 = 1) (hne : ℓ ≠ p) (hn : 1 ≤ n) (hgen : IsPrimitiveRoot (p : ZMod (ℓ ^ n)) (Nat.totient (ℓ ^ n))) (r : ℕ) (hr : 1 ≤ r) : (x2611_14198_point_count (ℓ ^ n) p r : ℤ) = (p : ℤ) ^ r + 1 - ∑ j ∈ (Finset.Icc 1 n).filter (fun j => ℓ ^ (j - 1) * (ℓ - 1) ∣ r), ((ℓ ^ (j - 1) * (ℓ - 1) : ℕ) : ℤ) * (-1 : ℤ) ^ (r / (ℓ ^ (j - 1) * (ℓ - 1))) * (p : ℤ) ^ (r / 2)
statements.notes: Only the first assertion is selected; the Jacobian 2-primary torsion assertion is skipped. The equality is in ℤ to preserve ordinary subtraction. m_j is expanded. Natural r/2 is exact on every included summand, since m_j is divisible by 4; if r is odd the sum is empty, so no fractional exponent has been replaced incorrectly.

statements.label: Remark 5.5 (d = 25, p = 157)
statements.name: x2611_14198_remark5_5_157
statements.original:
For $\ell=5$ and $p=13$ , Theorem 1.2 gives
 $L_{\mathcal{H}_{25},13}(T)=(1+13^{2}T^{4})(1+13^{10}T^{20})$ , where
 $L_{C,p}(T)=T^{2g}P_{C,p}(T^{-1})$ , and similarly for $\mathcal{H}_{125}$ ; these
recover the computations in [17, Example 4.2.8].

The necessity direction is already visible at the next type of examples. For
 $d=25$ and $p=157$ , the prime $157$ is a primitive root modulo $5$ but not
modulo $25$ (its order modulo $25$ is $4$ ), so
Proposition 4.4 excludes supersingularity of the
primitive factor $B_{2}$ and hence excludes maximality of $\mathcal{H}_{25}$ over every
finite extension of $\mathbb{F}_{157}$ . Likewise, if $d$ has two distinct prime
factors, Proposition 4.5 excludes supersingularity of $J_{d}$ in
characteristic $p\equiv 1\pmod{4}$ ; for example this applies to $d=65$ and
 $p=37$ .
statements.lean: [Fact (Nat.Prime 157)] : IsPrimitiveRoot (157 : ZMod 5) (Nat.totient 5) ∧ ¬ IsPrimitiveRoot (157 : ZMod 25) (Nat.totient 25) ∧ orderOf (157 : ZMod 25) = 4 ∧ ∀ r : ℕ, 1 ≤ r → ¬ x2611_14198_maximal 25 157 r
statements.notes: Selected the explicit p = 157 example: primitive modulo 5, not primitive modulo 25, exact order 4 modulo 25, and no maximal extension for H_25. Supersingularity of B₂ is excluded from this entry and listed in skipped. The numerical prime fact is exposed as an instance hypothesis so the concrete GaloisField is elaborated without constructing a proof.

statements.label: Corollary 6.2 and Table 1 (all maximal fields)
statements.name: x2611_14198_cor6_2_fields
statements.original:
Let $d\geq 3$ and let $p\nmid 2d$ be prime. Then $\mathcal{H}_{d}$ is maximal over
some finite extension of $\mathbb{F}_{p}$ if and only if one of the five cases in
Table 1 occurs. The last column of the table gives all
finite extensions over which it is maximal.
statements.lean: (d p r : ℕ) [Fact p.Prime] (hd : 3 ≤ d) (hcop : ¬ p ∣ 2 * d) (hr : 1 ≤ r) : x2611_14198_maximal d p r ↔ ((p % 4 = 1 ∧ Odd d ∧ ∃ ℓ a b : ℕ, ℓ.Prime ∧ ℓ % 4 = 1 ∧ 1 ≤ a ∧ d = ℓ ^ a ∧ IsPrimitiveRoot (p : ZMod (ℓ ^ a)) (Nat.totient (ℓ ^ a)) ∧ 1 ≤ b ∧ Odd b ∧ r = (ℓ ^ (a - 1) * (ℓ - 1)) * b) ∨ (p % 4 = 1 ∧ d % 4 = 2 ∧ ∃ ℓ a b : ℕ, ℓ.Prime ∧ ℓ % 4 = 1 ∧ 1 ≤ a ∧ d = 2 * ℓ ^ a ∧ IsPrimitiveRoot (p : ZMod (ℓ ^ a)) (Nat.totient (ℓ ^ a)) ∧ 1 ≤ b ∧ Odd b ∧ r = (ℓ ^ (a - 1) * (ℓ - 1)) * b) ∨ (p % 4 = 1 ∧ 4 ∣ d ∧ d = 4 ∧ p % 8 = 5 ∧ ∃ b : ℕ, 1 ≤ b ∧ Odd b ∧ r = 2 * b) ∨ (p % 4 = 3 ∧ Odd d ∧ (∃ k : ℕ, (p : ZMod (4 * d)) ^ k = -1 ∨ (p : ZMod (4 * d)) ^ k = ((1 + 2 * d : ℕ) : ZMod (4 * d))) ∧ ∃ b : ℕ, 1 ≤ b ∧ Odd b ∧ r = orderOf (p : ZMod (4 * d)) * b) ∨ (p % 4 = 3 ∧ Even d ∧ (∃ k : ℕ, (p : ZMod (2 * d)) ^ k = -1) ∧ ∃ b : ℕ, 1 ≤ b ∧ Odd b ∧ r = orderOf (p : ZMod (2 * d)) * b))
statements.notes: Expands the five table rows and the final column into one per-extension biconditional; this gives both existence and all maximal fields.
